Data Modeling Overview

1. How does Ignite store data?
  • Internally, every data entry is stored as a binary object in off-heap memory;
  • The entire dataset is divided into partitions, which are evenly distributed across server nodes;
  • Ignite provides two equivalent logical views of the same data:
    • Key-Value Cache — access data through a key-value API;
    • SQL Table — access data through standard SQL statements;
  • Both views read/write the same underlying data structure — you can mix them freely;
2. Key-Value Cache vs. SQL Table
Aspect Key-Value Cache SQL Table
Access pattern cache.get(key), cache.put(key, value) SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
Schema Optional (schemaless with binary objects) Required (columns, types, primary key)
Transactions Full ACID support DML in transactions (with limitations)
Joins Not applicable Distributed joins supported
Best for High-throughput point lookups Complex queries, aggregations, reporting
3. Physical vs. Logical Representation
  • Physical level:
    • Data is stored in off-heap memory pages (default 4 KB);
    • Pages are organized into partitions (1024 per cache by default);
    • Partitions are distributed across server nodes by the affinity function;
  • Logical level:
    • Applications see either a IgniteCache<K, V> (key-value) or a SQL table;
    • A SQL table with primary key id and columns name, age maps to a cache where the key is id and the value is an object with fields name and age;
4. Creating a Cache Programmatically
  • CacheConfiguration<Integer, String> cacheCfg = new CacheConfiguration<>("myCache");
cacheCfg.setCacheMode(CacheMode.PARTITIONED);
cacheCfg.setBackups(1);

IgniteCache<Integer, String> cache = ignite.getOrCreateCache(cacheCfg);
5. Creating a Table via SQL
  • CREATE TABLE Person (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR,
    age INT,
    city VARCHAR
) WITH "cache_name=PersonCache,template=partitioned,backups=1";
  • The WITH clause maps the SQL table to an Ignite cache and sets cache configuration parameters;
